texts.1ti.4.16: Tem cuidado de ti mesmo e da doutrina: persevera n’estas coisas; porque, fazendo isto, te salvarás, tanto a ti mesmo como aos que te ouvem.
texts.1ti.5.1: Não reprehendas asperamente os velhos, mas admoesta-os como a paes: aos mancebos como a irmãos.
texts.1ti.5.2: Ás velhas, como a mães, ás moças, como a irmãs, em toda a pureza.
texts.1ti.5.3: Honra as viuvas que verdadeiramente são viuvas.
texts.1ti.5.4: Mas, se alguma viuva tiver filhos, ou netos, aprendam primeiro a exercer piedade para com a sua propria familia, e a recompensar a seus paes; porque isto é bom e agradavel diante de Deus.
texts.1ti.5.5: Ora a que é verdadeiramente viuva e desamparada espera em Deus, e persevera de noite e de dia em rogos e orações;
texts.1ti.5.6: Mas a que vive em deleites, vivendo está morta.
texts.1ti.5.7: Manda, pois, estas coisas, para que sejam irreprehensiveis.
texts.1ti.5.8: Porém, se alguem não tem cuidado dos seus, e principalmente dos da sua familia, negou a fé, e é peior do que o infiel.
texts.1ti.5.9: Nunca se eleja viuva de menos de sessenta annos, e só a que tenha sido mulher de um marido;
texts.1ti.5.10: Tendo testemunho de boas obras: se criou os filhos, se exercitou hospitalidade, se lavou os pés aos sanctos, se soccorreu os afflictos, se seguiu toda a boa obra.
texts.1ti.5.11: Mas não admittas as viuvas moças, porque, havendo sido lascivas contra Christo, querem casar-se;
texts.1ti.5.12: Tendo já a sua condemnação por haverem aniquilado a primeira fé.
texts.1ti.5.13: E, além d’isto, tambem aprendem a andar ociosas de casa em casa; e não só ociosas, mas tambem paroleiras e curiosas, fallando o que não convem.
texts.1ti.5.14: Quero pois que as que são moças se casem, gerem filhos, governem a casa, e não dêem occasião alguma ao adversario de maldizer.
texts.1ti.5.15: Porque já algumas se desviaram, indo após Satanaz.
texts.1ti.5.16: Se algum crente ou alguma crente tem viuvas, soccorra-as, e não se sobrecarregue a egreja, para que possa sustentar as que deveras são viuvas.
texts.1ti.5.17: Os anciãos que governam bem sejam estimados por dignos de duplicada honra, principalmente os que trabalham na palavra e na doutrina.
texts.1ti.5.18: Porque diz a Escriptura: Não ligarás a bocca ao boi que debulha. E: Digno é o obreiro do seu salario.
texts.1ti.5.19: Não acceites accusação contra o ancião, senão com duas ou tres testemunhas.
texts.1ti.5.20: Aos que peccarem, reprehende-os na presença de todos, para que tambem os outros tenham temor.
texts.1ti.5.21: Conjuro-te diante de Deus, e do Senhor Jesus Christo, e dos anjos eleitos, que sem prejuizo algum guardes estas coisas, nada fazendo por parcialidade.
texts.1ti.5.22: A ninguem imponhas apressadamente as mãos, nem participes dos peccados alheios: conserva-te a ti mesmo puro.
texts.1ti.5.23: Não bebas mais agua sómente, mas usa tambem de um pouco de vinho; por causa do teu estomago e das tuas frequentes enfermidades.
texts.1ti.5.24: Os peccados de alguns homens são manifestos antes, e se adiantam para a sua condemnação; e em alguns manifestam-se ainda depois.
texts.1ti.5.25: Assim mesmo tambem as suas boas obras são manifestas, e as que são d’outra maneira não podem occultar-se.
texts.1ti.6.1: Todos os servos que estão debaixo do jugo estimem a seus senhores por dignos de toda a honra, para que o nome de Deus e a doutrina não sejam blasphemados.
texts.1ti.6.2: E os que teem senhores fieis não os desprezem, por serem irmãos; antes os sirvam melhor, porquanto são fieis e amados, como tambem participantes d’este beneficio. Isto ensina e exhorta.
texts.1ti.6.3: Se alguem ensina alguma outra doutrina, e se não conforma com as sãs palavras de nosso Senhor Jesus Christo, e com a doutrina que é conforme a piedade,
texts.1ti.6.4: É soberbo, e nada sabe, mas delira ácerca de questões e contendas de palavras, das quaes nascem invejas, porfias, blasphemias, ruins suspeitas,
texts.1ti.6.5: Perversas contendas de homens corruptos de entendimento, e privados da verdade, cuidando que a piedade seja ganho; aparta-te dos taes.
texts.1ti.6.6: Grande ganho é, porém, a piedade com contentamento.
texts.1ti.6.7: Porque nada trouxemos para este mundo, e manifesto é que nada podemos levar d’elle.
texts.1ti.6.8: Tendo, porém, sustento, e com que nos cobrirmos, estejamos com isso contentes.
texts.1ti.6.9: Mas os que querem ser ricos caem em tentação e em laço, e em muitas concupiscencias loucas e nocivas, que submergem os homens na perdição e ruina,
texts.1ti.6.10: Porque o amor do dinheiro é a raiz de todos os males; o que apetecendo alguns, se desviaram da fé, e se traspassaram a si mesmos com muitas dôres.
texts.1ti.6.11: Mas tu, ó homem de Deus, foge d’estas coisas, e segue a justiça, a piedade, a fé, a caridade, a paciencia, a mansidão.
texts.1ti.6.12: Milita a boa milicia da fé, lança mão da vida eterna, para a qual tambem foste chamado, tendo já feito boa confissão diante de muitas testemunhas.
texts.1ti.6.13: Mando-te diante de Deus, que todas as coisas vivifica, e de Christo Jesus, que diante de Poncio Pilatos testificou boa confissão,
texts.1ti.6.14: Que guardes este mandamento sem macula e reprehensão, até á apparição de nosso Senhor Jesus Christo;
texts.1ti.6.15: O qual a seu tempo mostrará o bemaventurado, e só poderoso Senhor, Rei dos reis e Senhor dos senhores;
texts.1ti.6.16: Aquelle que é só o que tem a immortalidade, e habita na luz inaccessivel; a quem nenhum dos homens viu nem pode vêr: ao qual seja honra e poder sempiterno. Amen.
texts.1ti.6.17: Manda aos ricos d’este mundo que não sejam altivos, nem ponham a esperança na incerteza das riquezas, mas em Deus vivo, que abundantemente nos dá todas as coisas para d’ellas gozarmos:
texts.1ti.6.18: Que façam bem, enriqueçam em boas obras, repartam de boamente, e sejam communicaveis;
texts.1ti.6.19: Que enthesourem para si mesmo um bom fundamento para o futuro, para que possam alcançar a vida eterna.
texts.1ti.6.20: Ó Timotheo, guarda o deposito que te foi confiado, tendo horror aos clamores vãos e profanos e ás opposições da falsamente chamada sciencia;
texts.1ti.6.21: A qual professando alguns, se desviaram da fé. A graça seja comtigo. Amen.

texts.1ti.1.1: Paul, an apostle of Jesus Christ by the commandment of God our Savior, and Lord Jesus Christ, who is our hope;
texts.1ti.1.2: To Timothy, my own son in the faith: Grace, mercy, and peace, from God our Father and Jesus Christ our Lord.
texts.1ti.1.3: As I besought thee to abide still at Ephesus, when I went into Macedonia, that thou mightest charge some that they teach no other doctrine,
texts.1ti.1.4: Neither give heed to fables and endless genealogies, which minister questions, rather than godly edifying which is in faith; so do.
texts.1ti.1.5: Now the end of the commandment is charity out of a pure heart, and of a good conscience, and of faith unfeigned:
texts.1ti.1.6: From which some having swerved, have turned aside to vain jangling;
texts.1ti.1.7: Desiring to be teachers of the law; understanding neither what they say, nor concerning what they affirm.
texts.1ti.1.8: But we know that the law is good, if a man useth it lawfully;
texts.1ti.1.9: Knowing this, that the law is not made for a righteous man, but for the lawless and disobedient, for the ungodly and for sinners, for unholy and profane, for murderers of fathers, and murderers of mothers, for man-slayers,
texts.1ti.1.10: For lewd persons, for them that defile themselves with mankind, for men-stealers, for liars, for perjured persons, and if there is any other thing that is contrary to sound doctrine,
texts.1ti.1.11: According to the glorious gospel of the blessed God, which was committed to my trust.
texts.1ti.1.12: And I thank Christ Jesus our Lord, who hath enabled me, for that he counted me faithful, putting me into the ministry;
texts.1ti.1.13: Who was before a blasphemer, and a persecutor, and injurious: but I obtained mercy, because I did it ignorantly in unbelief:
texts.1ti.1.14: And the grace of our Lord was exceeding abundant with faith and love which is in Christ Jesus.
texts.1ti.1.15: This is a faithful saying, and worthy of all acceptation, that Christ Jesus came into the world to save sinners; of whom I am chief.
texts.1ti.1.16: However, for this cause I obtained mercy, that in me first Jesus Christ might show forth all long-suffering, for a pattern to them who should hereafter believe on him to life everlasting.
texts.1ti.1.17: Now to the King eternal, immortal, invisible, God the only wise, be honor and glory for ever and ever. Amen.
texts.1ti.1.18: This charge I commit to thee, son Timothy, according to the prophecies which went before on thee, that thou by them mayest war a good warfare;
texts.1ti.1.19: Holding faith and a good conscience; which some having put away, concerning faith have made shipwreck:
texts.1ti.1.20: Of whom is Hymeneus and Alexander; whom I have delivered to Satan, that they may learn not to blaspheme.
texts.1ti.2.1: I exhort therefore, that first of all supplications, prayers, intercessions, and giving of thanks be made for all men;
texts.1ti.2.2: For kings, and for all that are in authority; that we may lead a quiet and peaceable life in all godliness and honesty.
texts.1ti.2.3: For this is good and acceptable in the sight of God our Savior;
texts.1ti.2.4: Who will have all men to be saved, and to come to the knowledge of the truth.
texts.1ti.2.5: For there is one God, and one mediator between God and men, the man Christ Jesus;
texts.1ti.2.6: Who gave himself a ransom for all, to be testified in due time.
texts.1ti.2.7: For which I am ordained a preacher and an apostle, (I speak the truth in Christ, and lie not) a teacher of the Gentiles in faith and verity.
texts.1ti.2.8: I will therefore that men pray every where, lifting up holy hands, without wrath and doubting.
texts.1ti.2.9: In like manner also, that women adorn themselves in decent apparel, with modesty and sobriety; not with broidered hair, or gold, or pearls, or costly array,
texts.1ti.2.10: But (which becometh women professing godliness) with good works.
texts.1ti.2.11: Let the woman learn in silence with all subjection.
texts.1ti.2.12: But I suffer not a woman to teach, nor to usurp authority over the man, but to be in silence.
texts.1ti.2.13: For Adam was first formed, then Eve.
texts.1ti.2.14: And Adam was not deceived, but the woman being deceived was in the transgression.
texts.1ti.2.15: Notwithstanding, she will be saved in child-bearing, if they continue in faith, and charity, and holiness, with sobriety.
texts.1ti.3.1: This is a true saying, If a man desireth the office of a bishop, he desireth a good work.
texts.1ti.3.2: A bishop then must be blameless, the husband of one wife, vigilant, sober, of good behavior, given to hospitality, apt to teach;
texts.1ti.3.3: Not given to wine, no striker, not greedy of filthy lucre, but patient; not a brawler, not covetous;
texts.1ti.3.4: One that ruleth well his own house, having his children in subjection with all gravity;
texts.1ti.3.5: (For if a man knoweth not how to rule his own house, how shall he take care of the church of God?)
texts.1ti.3.6: Not a novice, lest being lifted up with pride he fall into the condemnation of the devil.
texts.1ti.3.7: Moreover, he must have a good report of them who are without; lest he fall into reproach and the snare of the devil.
texts.1ti.3.8: Likewise must the deacons be grave, not double-tongued, not given to much wine, not greedy of filthy lucre,
texts.1ti.3.9: Holding the mystery of the faith in a pure conscience.
texts.1ti.3.10: And let these also first be proved; then let them use the office of a deacon, being found blameless.
texts.1ti.3.11: Even so must their wives be grave, not slanderers, sober, faithful in all things.
texts.1ti.3.12: Let the deacons be the husbands of one wife, ruling their children, and their own houses well.
texts.1ti.3.13: For they that have used the office of a deacon well, purchase to themselves a good degree, and great boldness in the faith, which is in Christ Jesus.
texts.1ti.3.14: These things I write to thee, hoping to come to thee shortly:
texts.1ti.3.15: But if I tarry long, that thou mayest know how thou oughtest to behave thyself in the house of God, which is the church of the living God, the pillar and ground of the truth.
texts.1ti.3.16: And without controversy, great is the mystery of godliness: God was manifest in the flesh, justified in the Spirit, seen by angels, preached to the Gentiles, believed on in the world, received up into glory.
texts.1ti.4.1: Now the Spirit speaketh expressly, that in the latter times some will depart from the faith, giving heed to seducing spirits and doctrines of demons;
texts.1ti.4.2: Speaking lies in hypocrisy, having their conscience seared with a hot iron;
texts.1ti.4.3: Forbidding to marry, and commanding to abstain from meats, which God hath created to be received with thanksgiving by them who believe and know the truth.
texts.1ti.4.4: For every creature of God is good, and nothing to be refused, if received with thanksgiving:
texts.1ti.4.5: For it is sanctified by the word of God, and prayer.
texts.1ti.4.6: If thou shalt put the brethren in remembrance of these things, thou wilt be a good minister of Jesus Christ, nourished by the words of faith and of good doctrine, to which thou hast attained.
texts.1ti.4.7: But refuse profane and old wives' fables, and exercise thyself rather to godliness.
texts.1ti.4.8: For bodily exercise profiteth little: but godliness is profitable to all things, having promise of the life that now is, and of that which is to come.
texts.1ti.4.9: This is a faithful saying, and worthy of all acceptation.
texts.1ti.4.10: For therefore we both labor and suffer reproach, because we trust in the living God who is the Savior of all men, especially of those that believe.
texts.1ti.4.12: Let no man despise thy youth; but be thou an example of the believers, in word, in deportment, in charity, in spirit, in faith, in purity.
texts.1ti.4.13: Till I come, give attendance to reading, to exhortation, to doctrine.
texts.1ti.4.14: Neglect not the gift that is in thee, which was given thee by prophecy, with the laying on of the hands of the presbytery.
texts.1ti.4.15: Meditate upon these things; give thyself wholly to them; that thy profiting may appear to all.
texts.1ti.4.16: Take heed to thyself and to thy doctrine; continue in them: for in doing this thou wilt both save thyself, and them that hear thee.
texts.1ti.5.1: Rebuke not an elder, but entreat him as a father; and the younger men as brethren;
texts.1ti.5.2: The elder women as mothers; the younger as sisters, with all purity.
texts.1ti.5.3: Honor widows that are widows indeed.
texts.1ti.5.4: But if any widow hath children or nephews, let them learn first to show piety at home, and to requite their parents: for that is good and acceptable before God.
texts.1ti.5.5: Now she that is a widow indeed, and desolate, trusteth in God, and continueth in supplications and prayers night and day.
texts.1ti.5.6: But she that liveth in pleasure, is dead while she liveth.
texts.1ti.5.7: And these things give in charge, that they may be blameless.
texts.1ti.5.8: But if any provideth not for his own, and especially for those of his own house, he hath denied the faith, and is worse than an infidel.
texts.1ti.5.9: Let not a widow be taken into the number under sixty years old, having been the wife of one man.
texts.1ti.5.10: Well reported of for good works; if she hath brought up children, if she hath lodged strangers, if she hath washed the saints' feet, if she hath relieved the afflicted, if she hath diligently followed every good work.
texts.1ti.5.11: But the younger widows refuse: for when they have begun to grow wanton against Christ, they will marry;
texts.1ti.5.12: Having damnation, because they have cast off their first faith.
texts.1ti.5.13: And at the same time they learn to be idle, wandering about from house to house, and not only idle, but tattlers also, and busy-bodies, speaking things which they ought not.
texts.1ti.5.14: I will therefore that the younger women marry, bear children, guide the house, give no occasion to the adversary to speak reproachfully.
texts.1ti.5.15: For some are already turned aside after Satan.
texts.1ti.5.16: If any man or woman that believeth hath widows, let them relieve them, and let not the church be charged; that it may relieve them that are widows indeed.
texts.1ti.5.17: Let the elders that rule well, be counted worthy of double honor, especially they who labor in the word and doctrine.
texts.1ti.5.18: For the scripture saith, Thou shalt not muzzle the ox that treadeth out the corn. And, The laborer is worthy of his reward.
texts.1ti.5.19: Against an elder receive not an accusation, but before two or three witnesses.
texts.1ti.5.20: Them that sin rebuke before all, that others also may fear.
texts.1ti.5.21: I charge thee before God and the Lord Jesus Christ, and the elect angels, that thou observe these things without preferring one before another, doing nothing by partiality.
texts.1ti.5.22: Impose hands hastily on no man, neither be partaker of other men's sins: keep thyself pure.
texts.1ti.5.23: Drink no longer water, but use a little wine for thy stomach's sake, and thy frequent infirmities.
texts.1ti.5.24: Some men's sins are open beforehand, going before to judgment: and some men they follow after.
texts.1ti.5.25: Likewise also the good works of some are manifest beforehand; and they that are otherwise cannot be hid.
texts.1ti.6.1: Let as many servants as are under the yoke count their own masters worthy of all honor, that the name of God and his doctrine may not be blasphemed.
texts.1ti.6.2: And they that have believing masters, let them not despise them, because they are brethren; but rather do them service, because they are faithful and beloved, partakers of the benefit. These things teach and exhort.
texts.1ti.6.3: If any man teacheth otherwise, and consenteth not to wholesome words, even the words of our Lord Jesus Christ, and the doctrine which is according to godliness,
texts.1ti.6.4: He is proud, knowing nothing, but doting about questions and strifes of words, from which cometh envy, strife, railings, evil surmisings,
texts.1ti.6.5: Perverse disputings of men of corrupt minds, and destitute of the truth, supposing gain to be godliness: from such withdraw thyself.
texts.1ti.6.6: But godliness with contentment is great gain.
texts.1ti.6.7: For we brought nothing into this world, and it is certain we can carry nothing out.
texts.1ti.6.8: And having food and raiment, with these let us be content.
texts.1ti.6.9: But they that will be rich, fall into temptation, and a snare, and into many foolish and hurtful lusts, which drown men in destruction and perdition.
texts.1ti.6.10: For the love of money is the root of all evil: which while some have coveted, they have erred from the faith, and pierced themselves through with many sorrows.
texts.1ti.6.11: But thou, O man of God, flee from these things; and follow after righteousness, godliness, faith, love, patience, meekness.
texts.1ti.6.12: Fight the good fight of faith, lay hold on eternal life, to which thou art also called, and hast professed a good profession before many witnesses.
texts.1ti.6.13: I give thee charge in the sight of God, who maketh alive all things, and before Christ Jesus, who before Pontius Pilate testified a good confession;
texts.1ti.6.14: That thou keep this commandment without spot, unrebukable, until the appearing of our Lord Jesus Christ:
texts.1ti.6.15: Which in his times he will show who is the blessed and only Potentate, the King of kings, and Lord of lords;
texts.1ti.6.16: Who only hath immortality, dwelling in the light which no man can approach; whom no man hath seen, nor can see: to whom be honor and power everlasting. Amen.
texts.1ti.6.17: Charge them that are rich in this world, that they be not high-minded, nor trust in uncertain riches, but in the living God, who giveth us richly all things to enjoy;
texts.1ti.6.18: That they do good, that they be rich in good works, ready to distribute, willing to communicate;
texts.1ti.6.19: Laying up in store for themselves a good foundation against the time to come, that they may lay hold on eternal life.
texts.1ti.6.20: O Timothy, keep that which is committed to thy trust, avoiding profane and vain babblings, and oppositions of science falsely so called;
texts.1ti.6.21: Which some professing, have erred concerning the faith. Grace be with thee. Amen.

texts.1ti.1.1: Paul, apostle of Jesus Christ, according to [the] command of God our Saviour, and of Christ Jesus our hope,
texts.1ti.1.2: to Timotheus, [my] true child in faith: grace, mercy, peace, from God our Father and Christ Jesus our Lord.
texts.1ti.1.3: Even as I begged thee to remain in Ephesus, [when I was] going to Macedonia, that thou mightest enjoin some not to teach other doctrines,
texts.1ti.1.4: nor to turn their minds to fables and interminable genealogies, which bring questionings rather than [further] God's dispensation, which [is] in faith.
texts.1ti.1.5: But the end of what is enjoined is love out of a pure heart and a good conscience and unfeigned faith;
texts.1ti.1.6: which [things] some having missed, have turned aside to vain discourse,
texts.1ti.1.7: desiring to be law-teachers, not understanding either what they say or concerning what they [so] strenuously affirm.
texts.1ti.1.8: Now we know that the law [is] good if any one uses it lawfully,
texts.1ti.1.9: knowing this, that law has not its application to a righteous person, but to [the] lawless and insubordinate, to [the] impious and sinful, to [the] unholy and profane, to smiters of fathers and smiters of mothers; to murderers,
texts.1ti.1.10: fornicators, sodomites, kidnappers, liars, perjurers; and if any other thing is opposed to sound teaching,
texts.1ti.1.11: according to the glad tidings of the glory of the blessed God, with which *I* have been entrusted.
texts.1ti.1.12: [And] I thank Christ Jesus our Lord, who has given me power, that he has counted me faithful, appointing to ministry him
texts.1ti.1.13: who before was a blasphemer and persecutor, and an insolent overbearing [man]: but mercy was shewn me because I did it ignorantly, in unbelief.
texts.1ti.1.14: But the grace of our Lord surpassingly over-abounded with faith and love, which [is] in Christ Jesus.
texts.1ti.1.15: Faithful [is] the word, and worthy of all acceptation, that Christ Jesus came into the world to save sinners, of whom *I* am [the] first.
texts.1ti.1.16: But for this reason mercy was shewn me, that in me, [the] first, Jesus Christ might display the whole long-suffering, for a delineation of those about to believe on him to life eternal.
texts.1ti.1.17: Now to the King of the ages, [the] incorruptible, invisible, only God, honour and glory to the ages of ages. Amen.
texts.1ti.1.18: This charge, [my] child Timotheus, I commit to thee, according to the prophecies as to thee preceding, in order that thou mightest war by them the good warfare,
texts.1ti.1.19: maintaining faith and a good conscience; which [last] some, having put away, have made shipwreck as to faith;
texts.1ti.1.20: of whom is Hymenaeus and Alexander, whom I have delivered to Satan, that they may be taught by discipline not to blaspheme.
texts.1ti.2.1: I exhort therefore, first of all, that supplications, prayers, intercessions, thanksgivings be made for all men;
texts.1ti.2.2: for kings and all that are in dignity, that we may lead a quiet and tranquil life in all piety and gravity;
texts.1ti.2.3: for this is good and acceptable before our Saviour God,
texts.1ti.2.4: who desires that all men should be saved and come to [the] knowledge of [the] truth.
texts.1ti.2.5: For God is one, and [the] mediator of God and men one, [the] man Christ Jesus,
texts.1ti.2.6: who gave himself a ransom for all, the testimony [to be rendered] in its own times;
texts.1ti.2.7: to which *I* have been appointed a herald and apostle, (I speak [the] truth, I do not lie,) a teacher of [the] nations in faith and truth.
texts.1ti.2.8: I will therefore that the men pray in every place, lifting up pious hands, without wrath or reasoning.
texts.1ti.2.9: In like manner also that the women in decent deportment and dress adorn themselves with modesty and discretion, not with plaited [hair] and gold, or pearls, or costly clothing,
texts.1ti.2.10: but, what becomes women making profession of the fear of God, by good works.
texts.1ti.2.11: Let a woman learn in quietness in all subjection;
texts.1ti.2.12: but I do not suffer a woman to teach nor to exercise authority over man, but to be in quietness;
texts.1ti.2.13: for Adam was formed first, then Eve:
texts.1ti.2.14: and Adam was not deceived; but the woman, having been deceived, was in transgression.
texts.1ti.2.15: But she shall be preserved in childbearing, if they continue in faith and love and holiness with discretion.
texts.1ti.3.1: The word [is] faithful: if any one aspires to exercise oversight, he desires a good work.
texts.1ti.3.2: The overseer then must be irreproachable, husband of one wife, sober, discreet, decorous, hospitable, apt to teach;
texts.1ti.3.3: not given to excesses from wine, not a striker, but mild, not addicted to contention, not fond of money,
texts.1ti.3.4: conducting his own house well, having [his] children in subjection with all gravity;
texts.1ti.3.5: (but if one does not know how to conduct his own house, how shall he take care of the assembly of God?)
texts.1ti.3.6: not a novice, that he may not, being inflated, fall into [the] fault of the devil.
texts.1ti.3.7: But it is necessary that he should have also a good testimony from those without, that he may fall not into reproach and [the] snare of the devil.
texts.1ti.3.8: Ministers, in like manner, grave, not double-tongued, not given to much wine, not seeking gain by base means,
texts.1ti.3.9: holding the mystery of the faith in a pure conscience.
texts.1ti.3.10: And let these be first proved, then let them minister, being without charge [against them].
texts.1ti.3.11: [The] women in like manner grave, not slanderers, sober, faithful in all things.
texts.1ti.3.12: Let [the] ministers be husbands of one wife, conducting [their] children and their own houses well:
texts.1ti.3.13: for those who shall have ministered well obtain for themselves a good degree, and much boldness in faith which [is] in Christ Jesus.
texts.1ti.3.14: These things I write to thee, hoping to come to thee more quickly;
texts.1ti.3.15: but if I delay, in order that thou mayest know how one ought to conduct oneself in God's house, which is [the] assembly of [the] living God, [the] pillar and base of the truth.
texts.1ti.3.16: And confessedly the mystery of piety is great. God has been manifested in flesh, has been justified in [the] Spirit, has appeared to angels, has been preached among [the] nations, has been believed on in [the] world, has been received up in glory.
texts.1ti.4.1: But the Spirit speaks expressly, that in latter times some shall apostatise from the faith, giving their mind to deceiving spirits and teachings of demons
texts.1ti.4.2: speaking lies in hypocrisy, cauterised as to their own conscience,
texts.1ti.4.3: forbidding to marry, [bidding] to abstain from meats, which God has created for receiving with thanksgiving for them who are faithful and know the truth.
texts.1ti.4.4: For every creature of God [is] good, and nothing [is] to be rejected, being received with thanksgiving;
texts.1ti.4.5: for it is sanctified by God's word and freely addressing [him].
texts.1ti.4.6: Laying these things before the brethren, thou wilt be a good minister of Christ Jesus, nourished with the words of the faith and of the good teaching which thou hast fully followed up.
texts.1ti.4.7: But profane and old wives' fables avoid, but exercise thyself unto piety;
texts.1ti.4.8: for bodily exercise is profitable for a little, but piety is profitable for everything, having promise of life, of the present one, and of that to come.
texts.1ti.4.9: The word [is] faithful and worthy of all acceptation;
texts.1ti.4.10: for, for this we labour and suffer reproach, because we hope in a living God, who is preserver of all men, specially of those that believe.
texts.1ti.4.12: Let no one despise thy youth, but be a model of the believers, in word, in conduct, in love, in faith, in purity.
texts.1ti.4.13: Till I come, give thyself to reading, to exhortation, to teaching.
texts.1ti.4.14: Be not negligent of the gift [that is] in thee, which has been given to thee through prophecy, with imposition of the hands of the elderhood.
texts.1ti.4.15: Occupy thyself with these things; be wholly in them, that thy progress may be manifest to all.
texts.1ti.4.16: Give heed to thyself and to the teaching; continue in them; for, doing this, thou shalt save both thyself and those that hear thee.
texts.1ti.5.1: Rebuke not an elder sharply, but exhort [him] as a father, younger [men] as brethren,
texts.1ti.5.2: elder women as mothers, younger women as sisters, with all purity.
texts.1ti.5.3: Honour widows who are really widows;
texts.1ti.5.4: but if any widow have children or descendants, let them learn first to be pious as regards their own house, and to render a return on their side to [their] parents; for this is acceptable in the sight of God.
texts.1ti.5.5: Now she who [is] a widow indeed, and is left alone, has put [her] hope in God, and continues in supplications and prayers night and day.
texts.1ti.5.6: But she that lives in habits of self-indulgence is dead [while] living.
texts.1ti.5.7: And these things enjoin, that they may be irreproachable.
texts.1ti.5.8: But if any one does not provide for his own, and specially for those of [his] house, he has denied the faith, and is worse than the unbeliever.
texts.1ti.5.9: Let a widow be put upon the list, being of not less than sixty years, [having been] wife of one man,
texts.1ti.5.10: borne witness to in good works, if she have brought up children, if she have exercised hospitality, if she have washed saints' feet, if she have imparted relief to the distressed, if she have diligently followed every good work.
texts.1ti.5.11: But younger widows decline; for when they grow wanton against Christ, they desire to marry,
texts.1ti.5.12: being guilty, because they have cast off their first faith.
texts.1ti.5.13: And, at the same time, they learn also [to be] idle, going about to people's houses; and not only idle, but also gossipers and meddlers, speaking things not becoming.
texts.1ti.5.14: I will therefore that the younger marry, bear children, rule the house, give no occasion to the adversary in respect of reproach.
texts.1ti.5.15: For already some have turned aside after Satan.
texts.1ti.5.16: If any believing man or woman have widows, let them impart relief to them, and let not the assembly be charged, that it may impart relief to those [that are] widows indeed.
texts.1ti.5.17: Let the elders who take the lead [among the saints] well be esteemed worthy of double honour, specially those labouring in word and teaching;
texts.1ti.5.18: for the scripture says, Thou shalt not muzzle an ox that treadeth out corn, and, The workman [is] worthy of his hire.
texts.1ti.5.19: Against an elder receive not an accusation unless where there are two or three witnesses.
texts.1ti.5.20: Those that sin convict before all, that the rest also may have fear.
texts.1ti.5.21: I testify before God and Christ Jesus and the elect angels, that thou keep these things without prejudice, doing nothing by favour.
texts.1ti.5.22: Lay hands quickly on no man, nor partake in others' sins. Keep thyself pure.
texts.1ti.5.23: Drink no longer only water, but use a little wine on account of thy stomach and thy frequent illnesses.
texts.1ti.5.24: Of some men the sins are manifest beforehand, going before to judgment, and some also they follow after.
texts.1ti.5.25: In like manner good works also are manifest beforehand, and those that are otherwise cannot be hid.
texts.1ti.6.1: Let as many bondmen as are under yoke count their own masters worthy of all honour, that the name of God and the teaching be not blasphemed.
texts.1ti.6.2: And they that have believing masters, let them not despise [them] because they are brethren; but let them the rather serve them with subjection, because they are faithful and beloved, who profit by the good and ready service [rendered]. These things teach and exhort.
texts.1ti.6.3: If any one teach differently, and do not accede to sound words, those of our Lord Jesus Christ, and the teaching which [is] according to piety,
texts.1ti.6.4: he is puffed up, knowing nothing, but sick about questions and disputes of words, out of which arise envy, strife, injurious words, evil suspicions,
texts.1ti.6.5: constant quarrellings of men corrupted in mind and destitute of the truth, holding gain to be [the end of] piety.
texts.1ti.6.6: But piety with contentment *is* great gain.
texts.1ti.6.7: For we have brought nothing into the world: [it is] [manifest] that neither can we carry anything out.
texts.1ti.6.8: But having sustenance and covering, we will be content with these.
texts.1ti.6.9: But those who desire to be rich fall into temptation and a snare, and many unwise and hurtful lusts, which plunge men into destruction and ruin.
texts.1ti.6.10: For the love of money is [the] root of every evil; which some having aspired after, have wandered from the faith, and pierced themselves with many sorrows.
texts.1ti.6.11: But *thou*, O man of God, flee these things, and pursue righteousness, piety, faith, love, endurance, meekness of spirit.
texts.1ti.6.12: Strive earnestly [in] the good conflict of faith. Lay hold of eternal life, to which thou hast been called, and hast confessed the good confession before many witnesses.
texts.1ti.6.13: I enjoin thee before God who preserves all things in life, and Christ Jesus who witnessed before Pontius Pilate the good confession,
texts.1ti.6.14: that thou keep the commandment spotless, irreproachable, until the appearing of our Lord Jesus Christ;
texts.1ti.6.15: which in its own time the blessed and only Ruler shall shew, the King of those that reign, and Lord of those that exercise lordship;
texts.1ti.6.16: who only has immortality, dwelling in unapproachable light; whom no man has seen, nor is able to see; to whom [be] honour and eternal might. Amen.
texts.1ti.6.17: Enjoin on those rich in the present age not to be high-minded, nor to trust on the uncertainty of riches; but in the God who affords us all things richly for [our] enjoyment;
texts.1ti.6.18: to do good, to be rich in good works, to be liberal in distributing, disposed to communicate [of their substance],
texts.1ti.6.19: laying by for themselves a good foundation for the future, that they may lay hold of [what is] really life.
texts.1ti.6.20: O Timotheus, keep the entrusted deposit, avoiding profane, vain babblings, and oppositions of false-named knowledge,
texts.1ti.6.21: of which some having made profession, have missed the faith. Grace [be] with thee.

texts.1ti.1.1: Paul, an apostle of Jesus Christ, according to a command of God our Saviour, and of the Lord Jesus Christ our hope,
texts.1ti.1.2: to Timotheus -- genuine child in faith: Grace, kindness, peace, from God our Father, and Christ Jesus our Lord,
texts.1ti.1.3: according as I did exhort thee to remain in Ephesus -- I going on to Macedonia -- that thou mightest charge certain not to teach any other thing,
texts.1ti.1.4: nor to give heed to fables and endless genealogies, that cause questions rather than the building up of God that is in faith: --
texts.1ti.1.5: And the end of the charge is love out of a pure heart, and of a good conscience, and of faith unfeigned,
texts.1ti.1.6: from which certain, having swerved, did turn aside to vain discourse,
texts.1ti.1.7: willing to be teachers of law, not understanding either the things they say, nor concerning what they asseverate,
texts.1ti.1.8: and we have known that the law [is] good, if any one may use it lawfully;
texts.1ti.1.9: having known this, that for a righteous man law is not set, but for lawless and insubordinate persons, ungodly and sinners, impious and profane, parricides and matricides, men-slayers,
texts.1ti.1.10: whoremongers, sodomites, men-stealers, liars, perjured persons, and if there be any other thing that to sound doctrine is adverse,
texts.1ti.1.11: according to the good news of the glory of the blessed God, with which I was entrusted.
texts.1ti.1.12: And I give thanks to him who enabled me -- Christ Jesus our Lord -- that he did reckon me stedfast, having put [me] to the ministration,
texts.1ti.1.13: who before was speaking evil, and persecuting, and insulting, but I found kindness, because, being ignorant, I did [it] in unbelief,
texts.1ti.1.14: and exceedingly abound did the grace of our Lord, with faith and love that [is] in Christ Jesus:
texts.1ti.1.15: stedfast [is] the word, and of all acceptation worthy, that Christ Jesus came to the world to save sinners -- first of whom I am;
texts.1ti.1.16: but because of this I found kindness, that in me first Jesus Christ might shew forth all long-suffering, for a pattern of those about to believe on him to life age-during:
texts.1ti.1.17: and to the King of the ages, the incorruptible, invisible, only wise God, [is] honour and glory -- to the ages of the ages! Amen.
texts.1ti.1.18: This charge I commit to thee, child Timotheus, according to the prophesies that went before upon thee, that thou mayest war in them the good warfare,
texts.1ti.1.19: having faith and a good conscience, which certain having thrust away, concerning the faith did make shipwreck,
texts.1ti.1.20: of whom are Hymenaeus and Alexander, whom I did deliver to the Adversary, that they might be instructed not to speak evil.
texts.1ti.2.1: I exhort, then, first of all, there be made supplications, prayers, intercessions, thanksgivings, for all men:
texts.1ti.2.2: for kings, and all who are in authority, that a quiet and peaceable life we may lead in all piety and gravity,
texts.1ti.2.3: for this [is] right and acceptable before God our Saviour,
texts.1ti.2.4: who doth will all men to be saved, and to come to the full knowledge of the truth;
texts.1ti.2.5: for one [is] God, one also [is] mediator of God and of men, the man Christ Jesus,
texts.1ti.2.6: who did give himself a ransom for all -- the testimony in its own times --
texts.1ti.2.7: in regard to which I was set a preacher and apostle -- truth I say in Christ, I do not lie -- a teacher of nations, in faith and truth.
texts.1ti.2.8: I wish, therefore, that men pray in every place, lifting up kind hands, apart from anger and reasoning;
texts.1ti.2.9: in like manner also the women, in becoming apparel, with modesty and sobriety to adorn themselves, not in braided hair, or gold, or pearls, or garments of great price,
texts.1ti.2.10: but -- which becometh women professing godly piety -- through good works.
texts.1ti.2.11: Let a woman in quietness learn in all subjection,
texts.1ti.2.12: and a woman I do not suffer to teach, nor to rule a husband, but to be in quietness,
texts.1ti.2.13: for Adam was first formed, then Eve,
texts.1ti.2.14: and Adam was not deceived, but the woman, having been deceived, into transgression came,
texts.1ti.2.15: and she shall be saved through the child-bearing, if they remain in faith, and love, and sanctification, with sobriety.
texts.1ti.3.1: Stedfast [is] the word: If any one the oversight doth long for, a right work he desireth;
texts.1ti.3.2: it behoveth, therefore, the overseer to be blameless, of one wife a husband, vigilant, sober, decent, a friend of strangers, apt to teach,
texts.1ti.3.3: not given to wine, not a striker, not given to filthy lucre, but gentle, not contentious, not a lover of money,
texts.1ti.3.4: his own house leading well, having children in subjection with all gravity,
texts.1ti.3.5: (and if any one his own house [how] to lead hath not known, how an assembly of God shall he take care of?)
texts.1ti.3.6: not a new convert, lest having been puffed up he may fall to a judgment of the devil;
texts.1ti.3.7: and it behoveth him also to have a good testimony from those without, that he may not fall into reproach and a snare of the devil.
texts.1ti.3.8: Ministrants -- in like manner grave, not double-tongued, not given to much wine, not given to filthy lucre,
texts.1ti.3.9: having the secret of the faith in a pure conscience,
texts.1ti.3.10: and let these also first be proved, then let them minister, being unblameable.
texts.1ti.3.11: Women -- in like manner grave, not false accusers, vigilant, faithful in all things.
texts.1ti.3.12: Ministrants -- let them be of one wife husbands; the children leading well, and their own houses,
texts.1ti.3.13: for those who did minister well a good step to themselves do acquire, and much boldness in faith that [is] in Christ Jesus.
texts.1ti.3.14: These things I write to thee, hoping to come unto thee soon,
texts.1ti.3.15: and if I delay, that thou mayest know how it behoveth [thee] to conduct thyself in the house of God, which is an assembly of the living God -- a pillar and foundation of the truth,
texts.1ti.3.16: and, confessedly, great is the secret of piety -- God was manifested in flesh, declared righteous in spirit, seen by messengers, preached among nations, believed on in the world, taken up in glory!
texts.1ti.4.1: And the Spirit expressly speaketh, that in latter times shall certain fall away from the faith, giving heed to seducing spirits and teachings of demons,
texts.1ti.4.2: in hypocrisy speaking lies, being seared in their own conscience,
texts.1ti.4.3: forbidding to marry -- to abstain from meats that God created to be received with thanksgiving by those believing and acknowledging the truth,
texts.1ti.4.4: because every creature of God [is] good, and nothing [is] to be rejected, with thanksgiving being received,
texts.1ti.4.5: for it is sanctified through the word of God and intercession.
texts.1ti.4.6: These things placing before the brethren, thou shalt be a good ministrant of Jesus Christ, being nourished by the words of the faith, and of the good teaching, which thou didst follow after,
texts.1ti.4.7: and the profane and old women's fables reject thou, and exercise thyself unto piety,
texts.1ti.4.8: for the bodily exercise is unto little profit, and the piety is to all things profitable, a promise having of the life that now is, and of that which is coming;
texts.1ti.4.9: stedfast [is] the word, and of all acceptation worthy;
texts.1ti.4.10: for for this we both labour and are reproached, because we hope on the living God, who is Saviour of all men -- especially of those believing.
texts.1ti.4.12: let no one despise thy youth, but a pattern become thou of those believing in word, in behaviour, in love, in spirit, in faith, in purity;
texts.1ti.4.13: till I come, give heed to the reading, to the exhortation, to the teaching;
texts.1ti.4.14: be not careless of the gift in thee, that was given thee through prophecy, with laying on of the hands of the eldership;
texts.1ti.4.15: of these things be careful; in these things be, that thy advancement may be manifest in all things;
texts.1ti.4.16: take heed to thyself, and to the teaching; remain in them, for this thing doing, both thyself thou shalt save, and those hearing thee.
texts.1ti.5.1: An aged person thou mayest not rebuke, but be entreating as a father; younger persons as brethren;
texts.1ti.5.2: aged women as mothers, younger ones as sisters -- in all purity;
texts.1ti.5.3: honour widows who are really widows;
texts.1ti.5.4: and if any widow have children or grandchildren, let them learn first to their own house to show piety, and to give back a recompense to the parents, for this is right and acceptable before God.
texts.1ti.5.5: And she who is really a widow and desolate, hath hoped upon God, and doth remain in the supplications and in the prayers night and day,
texts.1ti.5.6: and she who is given to luxury, living -- hath died;
texts.1ti.5.7: and these things charge, that they may be blameless;
texts.1ti.5.8: and if any one for his own -- and especially for those of the household -- doth not provide, the faith he hath denied, and than an unbeliever he is worse.
texts.1ti.5.9: A widow -- let her not be enrolled under sixty years of age, having been a wife of one husband,
texts.1ti.5.10: in good works being testified to: if she brought up children, if she entertained strangers, if saints' feet she washed, if those in tribulation she relieved, if every good work she followed after;
texts.1ti.5.11: and younger widows be refusing, for when they may revel against the Christ, they wish to marry,
texts.1ti.5.12: having judgment, because the first faith they did cast away,
texts.1ti.5.13: and at the same time also, they learn [to be] idle, going about the houses; and not only idle, but also tattlers and busybodies, speaking the things they ought not;
texts.1ti.5.14: I wish, therefore, younger ones to marry, to bear children, to be mistress of the house, to give no occasion to the opposer to reviling;
texts.1ti.5.15: for already certain did turn aside after the Adversary.
texts.1ti.5.16: If any believing man or believing woman have widows, let them relieve them, and let not the assembly be burdened, that those really widows it may relieve.
texts.1ti.5.17: The well-leading elders of double honour let them be counted worthy, especially those labouring in word and teaching,
texts.1ti.5.18: for the Writing saith, `An ox treading out thou shalt not muzzle,' and `Worthy [is] the workman of his reward.'
texts.1ti.5.19: Against an elder an accusation receive not, except upon two or three witnesses.
texts.1ti.5.20: Those sinning, reprove before all, that the others also may have fear;
texts.1ti.5.21: I testify fully, before God and the Lord Jesus Christ, and the choice messengers, that these things thou mayest keep, without forejudging, doing nothing by partiality.
texts.1ti.5.22: Be laying hands quickly on no one, nor be having fellowship with sins of others; be keeping thyself pure;
texts.1ti.5.23: no longer be drinking water, but a little wine be using, because of thy stomach and of thine often infirmities;
texts.1ti.5.24: of certain men the sins are manifest beforehand, leading before to judgment, and certain also they follow after;
texts.1ti.5.25: in like manner also the right works are manifest beforehand, and those that are otherwise are not able to be hid.
texts.1ti.6.1: As many as are servants under a yoke, their own masters worthy of all honour let them reckon, that the name of God and the teaching may not be evil spoken of;
texts.1ti.6.2: and those having believing masters, let them not slight [them], because they are brethren, but rather let them serve, because they are stedfast and beloved, who of the benefit are partaking. These things be teaching and exhorting;
texts.1ti.6.3: if any one be teaching otherwise, and do not consent to sound words -- those of our Lord Jesus Christ -- and to the teaching according to piety,
texts.1ti.6.4: he is proud, knowing nothing, but doting about questions and word-striving, out of which doth come envy, strife, evil-speakings, evil-surmisings,
texts.1ti.6.5: wranglings of men wholly corrupted in mind, and destitute of the truth, supposing the piety to be gain; depart from such;
texts.1ti.6.6: but it is great gain -- the piety with contentment;
texts.1ti.6.7: for nothing did we bring into the world -- [it is] manifest that we are able to carry nothing out;
texts.1ti.6.8: but having food and raiment -- with these we shall suffice ourselves;
texts.1ti.6.9: and those wishing to be rich, do fall into temptation and a snare, and many desires, foolish and hurtful, that sink men into ruin and destruction,
texts.1ti.6.10: for a root of all the evils is the love of money, which certain longing for did go astray from the faith, and themselves did pierce through with many sorrows;
texts.1ti.6.11: and thou, O man of God, these things flee, and pursue righteousness, piety, faith, love, endurance, meekness;
texts.1ti.6.12: be striving the good strife of the faith, be laying hold on the life age-during, to which also thou wast called, and didst profess the right profession before many witnesses.
texts.1ti.6.13: I charge thee, before God, who is making all things alive, and of Christ Jesus, who did testify before Pontius Pilate the right profession,
texts.1ti.6.14: that thou keep the command unspotted, unblameable, till the manifestation of our Lord Jesus Christ,
texts.1ti.6.15: which in His own times He shall shew -- the blessed and only potentate, the King of the kings and Lord of the lords,
texts.1ti.6.16: who only is having immortality, dwelling in light unapproachable, whom no one of men did see, nor is able to see, to whom [is] honour and might age-during! Amen.
texts.1ti.6.17: Those rich in the present age charge thou not to be high-minded, nor to hope in the uncertainty of riches, but in the living God, who is giving to us all things richly for enjoyment; --
texts.1ti.6.18: to do good, to be rich in good works, to be ready to impart, willing to communicate,
texts.1ti.6.19: treasuring up to themselves a right foundation for the time to come, that they may lay hold on the life age-during.
texts.1ti.6.20: O Timotheus, the thing entrusted guard thou, avoiding the profane vain-words and opposition of the falsely-named knowledge,
texts.1ti.6.21: which certain professing -- concerning the faith did swerve; the grace [is] with you. Amen.

texts.1ti.1.1: Pablo, apóstol de Jesu Cristo por la ordenación de Dios Salvador nuestro, y del Señor Jesu Cristo, esperanza nuestra;
texts.1ti.1.2: A Timoteo, verdadero hijo mío en la fe: Gracia, misericordia, y paz de Dios nuestro Padre, y de Cristo Jesús nuestro Señor.
texts.1ti.1.3: Como te rogué, que te quedases en Efeso, cuando me partí para Macedonia, para que denunciases a algunos que no enseñen diversa doctrina:
texts.1ti.1.4: Ni escuchen a fábulas y genealogías interminables, que dan cuestiones más bien que edificación de Dios, que es en la fe: así házlo.
texts.1ti.1.5: Pues el fin del mandamiento es el amor nacido de corazón limpio, y de buena conciencia, y de fe no fingida:
texts.1ti.1.6: De lo cual apartándose algunos, se han desviado, dándose a discursos vanos:
texts.1ti.1.7: Queriendo ser doctores de la ley, y no entendiendo ni lo que hablan, ni lo que afirman.
texts.1ti.1.8: Mas sabemos que la ley es buena, si se usa de ella legítimamente:
texts.1ti.1.9: Sabiendo que la ley no es puesta para el justo, sino para los injustos, y para los desobedientes, para los impíos y pecadores, para los malos y contaminados, para los matadores de padres y de madres, para los homicidas,
texts.1ti.1.10: Para los fornicarios, para los que se contaminan con varones, para los ladrones de hombres, para los mentirosos y perjuros; y si hay alguna otra cosa contraria a la sana doctrina,
texts.1ti.1.11: Conforme al evangelio glorioso del Dios bienaventurado, el cual a mí me ha sido encargado.
texts.1ti.1.12: ¶ Gracias doy al que me fortificó, a Cristo Jesús Señor nuestro, de que me tuvo por fiel, poniéndome en el ministerio:
texts.1ti.1.13: Habiendo yo sido antes blasfemo, y perseguidor, e injuriador; mas fui recibido a misericordia, porque lo hice con ignorancia en incredulidad.
texts.1ti.1.14: Mas la gracia del Señor nuestro superabundó con la fe y amor que es en Cristo Jesús.
texts.1ti.1.15: Palabra fiel es esta, y digna de ser recibida de todos: que Cristo Jesús vino al mundo para salvar los pecadores, de los cuales yo soy el primero.
texts.1ti.1.16: Mas por esto fui recibido a misericordia, es a saber, para que Jesu Cristo mostrase en mí el primero toda su clemencia, para ejemplo de los que habían de creer en él para vida eterna.
texts.1ti.1.17: Al Rey de siglos, inmortal, invisible, al solo sabio Dios, sea honor y gloria por siglos de los siglos. Amén.
texts.1ti.1.18: ¶ Este mandamiento, hijo Timoteo, te encargo, para que conforme a las profecías pasadas de ti, milites por ellas buena milicia:
texts.1ti.1.19: Reteniendo la fe y una buena conciencia, la cual echando de sí algunos hicieron naufragio en la fe.
texts.1ti.1.20: De los cuales son Himeneo y Alejandro, que yo entregué a Satanás para que aprendan a no blasfemar.
texts.1ti.2.1: Amonesto, pues, ante todas cosas, que se hagan rogativas, oraciones, peticiones y acciones de gracias, por todos los hombres:
texts.1ti.2.2: Por los reyes, y por todos los que están en autoridad; que vivamos quieta y reposadamente en toda piedad y honestidad.
texts.1ti.2.3: Porque esto es bueno y agradable delante de Dios Salvador nuestro:
texts.1ti.2.4: El cual quiere que todos los hombres sean salvos, y que vengan al conocimiento de la verdad.
texts.1ti.2.5: Porque hay un Dios, y asimismo un solo mediador entre Dios y los hombres, el hombre Cristo Jesús;
texts.1ti.2.6: El cual se dio a sí mismo en precio del rescate por todos, para testimonio en su propio tiempo.
texts.1ti.2.7: Para lo que yo soy puesto por predicador y apóstol, (digo verdad en Cristo, no miento,) instruidor de las naciones en fe y verdad.
texts.1ti.2.8: Quiero, pues, que los varones oren en todo lugar, levantando manos limpias, sin ira ni contienda.
texts.1ti.2.9: ¶ Asimismo también oren las mujeres en hábito honesto, ataviándose de vergüenza y modestia; no con cabellos encrespados, o oro, o perlas, o vestidos costosos;
texts.1ti.2.10: Mas de buenas obras, como conviene a mujeres que profesan la piedad.
texts.1ti.2.11: ¶ La mujer aprenda en silencio con toda sujeción.
texts.1ti.2.12: Porque no permito a la mujer enseñar, ni tomarse autoridad sobre el varón, sino estar en silencio.
texts.1ti.2.13: Porque Adam fue formado el primero: luego Eva.
texts.1ti.2.14: Y Adam no fue engañado; mas la mujer siendo engañada incurrió en la prevaricación.
texts.1ti.2.15: Empero será salva engendrando hijos, si permaneciere en la fe y caridad, y en santificación y modestia.
texts.1ti.3.1: Palabra verdadera es esta: Si alguno apetece obispado, obra excelente desea.
texts.1ti.3.2: Es necesario, pues, que el obispo sea irreprensible, marido de una sola mujer, vigilante, templado, de buenas costumbres, hospedador, apto para enseñar,
texts.1ti.3.3: No amador del vino, no heridor, no codicioso de ganancias torpes, mas moderado, no pendenciero, ajeno de avaricia:
texts.1ti.3.4: Que gobierne bien su casa, que tenga sus hijos en sujeción con toda honestidad;
texts.1ti.3.5: Porque el que no sabe gobernar su casa, ¿cómo cuidará de la iglesia de Dios?
texts.1ti.3.6: No neófito, porque hinchándose de orgullo, no caiga en condenación del diablo.
texts.1ti.3.7: Y conviene que tenga también testimonio de los de afuera; porque no caiga en vituperio, y en lazo del diablo.
texts.1ti.3.8: ¶ Los diáconos asimismo sean honestos, no de dos lenguas, no dados a mucho vino, no amadores de torpes ganancias:
texts.1ti.3.9: Que tengan el misterio de la fe con limpia conciencia.
texts.1ti.3.10: Y estos también sean antes probados; y así ministren, si fueren hallados irreprensibles.
texts.1ti.3.11: Asimismo sus mujeres sean honestas, no detractoras, templadas, fieles en todo.
texts.1ti.3.12: Los diáconos sean maridos de una sola mujer, que gobiernen bien sus hijos, y sus casas.
texts.1ti.3.13: Porque los que ejercieren bien el oficio de diácono, ganan para sí un buen grado, y mucha confianza en la fe que es en Cristo Jesús.
texts.1ti.3.14: ¶ Esto te escribo, con esperanza de que vendré presto a ti:
texts.1ti.3.15: Y si no viniere tan presto, para que sepas como te convenga conversar en la casa de Dios, que es la iglesia del Dios vivo, columna y apoyo de la verdad.
texts.1ti.3.16: Y sin controversia grande es el misterio de la piedad: Dios ha sido manifestado en la carne; ha sido justificado en el Espíritu; ha sido visto de los ángeles; ha sido predicado entre las naciones; ha sido creído en el mundo; ha sido recibido en la gloria.
texts.1ti.4.1: Empero el Espíritu dice expresamente, que en los postreros tiempos algunos apostatarán de la fe, escuchando a espíritus engañadores, y a doctrinas de demonios,
texts.1ti.4.2: Que con hipocresía hablarán mentira, teniendo cauterizada la conciencia:
texts.1ti.4.3: Que prohibirán casarse, y obligarán a abstenerse los hombres de las viandas que Dios creó para que con hacimiento de gracias participasen de ellas los que creen, y conocen la verdad.
texts.1ti.4.4: Porque todo lo que Dios creó, es bueno, y nada hay que desechar, tomándose con hacimiento de gracias;
texts.1ti.4.5: Porque por la palabra de Dios, y por la oración es santificado.
texts.1ti.4.6: Si esto propusieres a los hermanos, serás buen ministro de Jesu Cristo, criado en las palabras de la fe, y de la buena doctrina, la cual has alcanzado.
texts.1ti.4.7: Mas las fábulas profanas y de viejas desecha, y ejercítate para la piedad.
texts.1ti.4.8: Porque el ejercicio corporal para poco es provechoso; mas la piedad a todo aprovecha; porque tiene la promesa de esta vida presente, y de la venidera.
texts.1ti.4.9: Palabra fiel es esta, y digna de ser recibida de todos.
texts.1ti.4.10: Que por esto aun trabajamos y somos maldichos, porque esperamos en el Dios viviente, el cual es Salvador de todos los hombres, y mayormente de los que creen.
texts.1ti.4.12: Ninguno tenga en poco tu juventud; mas sé ejemplo de los fieles en palabra, en conversación, en caridad, en espíritu, en fe, en pureza.
texts.1ti.4.13: Entre tanto que vengo, ocúpate en leer, en exhortar, en enseñar.
texts.1ti.4.14: No menosprecies el don que está en ti, que te es dado para profetizar, con la imposición de las manos de los presbíteros.
texts.1ti.4.15: Medita estas cosas; ocúpate cabalmente en ellas; de manera que tu aprovechamiento sea manifiesto a todos.
texts.1ti.4.16: Ten cuidado de ti mismo y de la doctrina: persiste en esto; porque si así lo hicieres, a ti mismo salvarás, y a los que te oyen.
texts.1ti.5.1: Al anciano no reprendas con dureza, mas exhórta le como a padre; a los jóvenes, como a hermanos;
texts.1ti.5.2: A las ancianas, como a madres; a las jóvenes, como a hermanas, con toda pureza:
texts.1ti.5.3: A las viudas honra, a las que de verdad son viudas:
texts.1ti.5.4: Empero si alguna viuda tuviere hijos, o nietos, aprendan primero a manifestar la piedad en casa, y a recompensar a sus padres; porque esto es honesto y acepto delante de Dios.
texts.1ti.5.5: Y la que de verdad es viuda y solitaria, espera en Dios, y persiste en suplicaciones y oraciones noche y día.
texts.1ti.5.6: Porque la que vive en delicias, viviendo está muerta.
texts.1ti.5.7: Denuncia pues estas cosas, para que sean irreprensibles.
texts.1ti.5.8: Mas si alguno no tiene cuidado de los suyos, y mayormente de los de su casa, ha negado la fe, y es peor que el infiel.
texts.1ti.5.9: La viuda sea puesta en oficio siendo no menos que de sesenta años, la cual haya sido mujer de un varón:
texts.1ti.5.10: Que tenga testimonio en buenas obras; si ha criado hijos; si ha hospedado; si ha lavado los pies de los santos; si ha socorrido a los que han padecido aflicción; si ha seguido toda buena obra.
texts.1ti.5.11: Mas a las viudas más mozas no admitas: que desde que han vivido disolutamente contra Cristo, quieren casarse:
texts.1ti.5.12: Condenadas ya, por haber abandonado la primera fe.
texts.1ti.5.13: Y asimismo también son ociosas, enseñadas a andar de casa en casa; y no solamente ociosas, empero aun parleras y curiosas, parlando lo que no conviene.
texts.1ti.5.14: Quiero, pues, que las mozas se casen, paran hijos, gobiernen la casa, y que ninguna ocasión den al adversario para decir mal.
texts.1ti.5.15: Porque ya algunas han vuelto atrás en pos de Satanás.
texts.1ti.5.16: Y si alguno, o alguna de los creyentes tiene viudas, manténgalas, y no sea cargada la iglesia; para que pueda socorrer a las que de verdad son viudas.
texts.1ti.5.17: ¶ Los ancianos que gobiernan bien, sean tenidos por dignos de doblada honra; y mayormente los que trabajan en la palabra y doctrina.
texts.1ti.5.18: Que la Escritura dice: No embozalarás al buey que trilla. Y: Digno es el obrero de su jornal.
texts.1ti.5.19: Contra el anciano no recibas acusación, sino ante dos o tres testigos.
texts.1ti.5.20: A los que pecaren repréndelos delante de todos, para que los otros también teman.
texts.1ti.5.21: Te requiero delante de Dios, y del Señor Jesu Cristo, y de sus ángeles escogidos, que guardes estas cosas sin preocupación, que nada hagas por parcialidad.
texts.1ti.5.22: No impongas ligeramente las manos sobre alguno, ni seas participante en pecados ajenos: consérvate puro a ti mismo.
texts.1ti.5.23: No bebas de aquí adelante agua, sino usa de un poco de vino por causa del estómago, y de tus continuas enfermedades.
texts.1ti.5.24: Los pecados de algunos hombres son manifiestos ya, yendo delante de ellos a juicio: a otros les vienen después.
texts.1ti.5.25: Asimismo también las buenas obras de algunos son manifiestas de antemano; y las que son de otra manera, no se pueden esconder.
texts.1ti.6.1: Todos los que están debajo de yugo de servidumbre, tengan a sus señores por dignos de toda honra, porque no sea blasfemado el nombre del Señor y su doctrina.
texts.1ti.6.2: Y los que tienen señores creyentes, no los tengan en menos, por ser sus hermanos; antes los sirvan mejor, por cuanto son fieles y amados, y partícipes del beneficio. Estas cosas enseña, y exhorta.
texts.1ti.6.3: ¶ Si alguno enseña de otra manera, y no se atiene a las sanas palabras de nuestro Señor Jesu Cristo, y a la doctrina que es conforme a la piedad,
texts.1ti.6.4: Hinchado es, nada sabe, sino que enloquece acerca de cuestiones y contiendas de palabras, de las cuales nacen envidias, pleitos, maledicencias, malas sospechas,
texts.1ti.6.5: Disputas perversas de hombres de corrompido entendimiento, y privados de la verdad, y que tienen la piedad por granjería: apártate de los que son tales.
texts.1ti.6.6: Grande granjería empero es la piedad, con el contentamiento de lo que basta.
texts.1ti.6.7: Porque nada trajimos al mundo, y sin duda nada podremos sacar.
texts.1ti.6.8: Así que teniendo sustento, y con que cubrirnos, seamos contentos con esto.
texts.1ti.6.9: Porque los que quieren ser ricos, caen en tentación y en lazo, y en muchas codicias insensatas y dañosas, que anegan a los hombres en perdición y muerte.
texts.1ti.6.10: Porque el amor del dinero es raíz de todos los males; el cual codiciando algunos erraron de la fe, y a sí mismos se traspasaron de muchos dolores.
texts.1ti.6.11: ¶ Mas tú, oh hombre de Dios, huye de estas cosas; y sigue la justicia, la piedad, la fe, el amor, la paciencia, la mansedumbre.
texts.1ti.6.12: Pelea la buena pelea de fe: echa mano de la vida eterna, a la cual asimismo eres llamado, habiendo hecho buena profesión delante de muchos testigos.
texts.1ti.6.13: ¶ Te mando delante de Dios, que da vida a todas las cosas, y de Jesu Cristo, que testificó una buena profesión delante de Poncio Pilato,
texts.1ti.6.14: Que guardes este mandamiento sin mácula, ni reprensión, hasta que aparezca el Señor nuestro Jesu Cristo:
texts.1ti.6.15: Al cual a su tiempo mostrará el bienaventurado y solo poderoso, Rey de reyes, y Señor de señores:
texts.1ti.6.16: Que solo tiene inmortalidad, que habita en luz a donde no se puede llegar: a quien ninguno de los hombres vio jamás, ni puede ver: al cual sea la honra, y el imperio sempiterno. Amén.
texts.1ti.6.17: ¶ A los ricos en este siglo manda que no sean altivos, ni pongan la esperanza en la incertidumbre de las riquezas; sino en el Dios vivo, que nos da todas las cosas en abundancia para que las gocemos.
texts.1ti.6.18: Que hagan bien, que sean ricos en buenas obras, prontos para repartir, comunicativos.
texts.1ti.6.19: Atesorando para sí buen fundamento para en lo porvenir, para que echen mano a la vida eterna.
texts.1ti.6.20: ¶ Oh Timoteo, guarda lo que se te ha encomendado, apartándote de las disputas profanas y vacías, y de las objeciones de la ciencia falsamente llamada así:
texts.1ti.6.21: La cual muchos profesando, han errado acerca de la fe. La gracia sea contigo. Amén. ¶ La primera a Timoteo fue escrita de Laodicea, que es metrópoli de la Frigia Pacatiana.

texts.1ti.1.1: Paul, an apostle of Christ Jesus—by injunction of God our Saviour and Christ Jesus our hope,—
texts.1ti.1.2: unto Timothy, my true child in faith: favour, mercy, peace, from God our Father, and Christ Jesus our Lord.
texts.1ti.1.3: Even as I exhorted thee to remain in Ephesus, when I was journeying into Macedonia, that thou mightest charge some—
texts.1ti.1.4: Not to be teaching otherwise, nor yet to be giving heed to stories and endless genealogies,—the which, bring, arguings, rather than that stewardship of God which is with faith;—
texts.1ti.1.5: Now, the end of the charge, is love—out of a pure heart, and a good conscience, and faith unfeigned,—
texts.1ti.1.6: Which some, missing, have turned them aside unto idle talk,
texts.1ti.1.7: Desiring to be law-teachers,—not understanding, either what they say or whereof they confidently affirm.
texts.1ti.1.8: Now we know that, excellent, is the law, if one put it to a lawful use:—
texts.1ti.1.9: Knowing this—that, to a righteous man, law, doth not apply, but to the lawless and insubordinate, ungodly and sinful, irreligious and profane, smiters of fathers and smiters of mothers, murderers,
texts.1ti.1.10: fornicators, sodomites, man-stealers, liars, false- swearers,—and, if anything else, unto the healthful teaching, is opposed;—
texts.1ti.1.11: According to the glad-message of the glory of the happy God, with which entrusted am, I.
texts.1ti.1.12: Grateful, am I unto him that empowered me, Christ Jesus our Lord, in that, faithful, he accounted me, putting me into ministry,—
texts.1ti.1.13: Though, formerly, a defamer, and persecutor, and insulter; nevertheless mercy was shown me, because, without knowledge, I acted, in unbelief:
texts.1ti.1.14: Yet exceeding abundant was the favour of our Lord, with faith and love which are in Christ Jesus.
texts.1ti.1.15: Faithful, the saying! and, of all acceptance, worthy,—that, Christ Jesus, came into the world, sinners, to save: of whom, the chief, am, I;—
texts.1ti.1.16: Nevertheless, on this account, was mercy shewn me,—that, in me, the chief, Christ Jesus might shew forth his entire longsuffering, for an ensample of them about to believe on him unto life age-abiding.
texts.1ti.1.17: Now, unto the King of the ages,—incorruptible, invisible, alone God, be honour and glory, unto the ages of ages, Amen!
texts.1ti.1.18: This charge, I commit unto thee, child Timothy, According to the prophecies, running before on thee, in order that thou mightest war, with them, the noble warfare.
texts.1ti.1.19: Holding faith and a good conscience,—which some, thrusting from them, concerning their faith, have made shipwreck:—
texts.1ti.1.20: Of whom are Hymenaeus and Alexander; whom I have delivered unto Satan, that they may be taught by discipline not to be defaming.
texts.1ti.2.1: I exhort, therefore, first of all, that there be made—supplications, prayers, intercessions, thankgivings, in behalf of all men,
texts.1ti.2.2: In behalf of kings, and all them who are, in eminent station; in order that, an undisturbed, and quiet life, we may lead, in all godliness and gravity:
texts.1ti.2.3: This, is comely and acceptable before our Saviour God,
texts.1ti.2.4: Who willeth, all men, to be saved, and, unto a personal knowledge of truth, to come;
texts.1ti.2.5: For there is, one, God, one, mediator also, between God and men,—a man—Christ Jesus:
texts.1ti.2.6: Who gave himself a ransom in behalf of all,—the testimony, in its own fit times:
texts.1ti.2.7: Unto which, I, have been appointed proclaimer and apostle—Truth I speak, I utter no falsehood—a teacher of nations, in faith and truth.
texts.1ti.2.8: I am minded, therefore, that—the men in every place be offering prayer, uplifting hands of lovingkindness, apart from anger and disputings;
texts.1ti.2.9: In the same way, that, the women, in seemly attire, with modesty and sober-mindedness, be adorning themselves,—not with plaitings and ornamentation of gold, or with pearls, or with costly apparel,—
texts.1ti.2.10: But, which becometh women promising godliness, through means of good works.
texts.1ti.2.11: Let, a woman, in quietness, be learning in all submission;
texts.1ti.2.12: But, teaching—unto a woman, I do not permit, nor yet to have authority over a man,—but to be in quietness;
texts.1ti.2.13: For, Adam, first was formed, then Eve,
texts.1ti.2.14: And, Adam, was not deceived, whereas, the woman, having been wholly deceived, hath come to be, in transgression;
texts.1ti.2.15: She shall be saved, however, through means of the child-bearing,—if they abide in faith, and love, and holiness, with sobermindedness. Faithful, the saying.
texts.1ti.3.1: If anyone, for oversight, is eager, a noble work, doth he covet:—
texts.1ti.3.2: It is needful, then, for, the overseer, to be irreproachable, a husband, of one wife, sober, of sound mind, orderly, hospitable, apt in teaching,
texts.1ti.3.3: Not given to wine, not ready to wound, but considerate, averse to contention, not fond of money,
texts.1ti.3.4: Over his own house, presiding, well, having, children, in submission, with all dignity;
texts.1ti.3.5: Whereas, if anyone, over his own house, cannot, preside, how, of an assembly of God, shall he take care?
texts.1ti.3.6: Not a new convert, lest, being beclouded, into the sentence of the adversary, he fall;
texts.1ti.3.7: It is needful, moreover, to have, an honourable testimony also, from them who are without, lest, into reproach, he fall, and the snare of the adversary.
texts.1ti.3.8: Ministers, in the same way,—dignified, not double-tongued, not, to much wine, given, not greedy of base gain,
texts.1ti.3.9: Holding the sacred secret of the faith in a pure conscience;
texts.1ti.3.10: But let, these also, be proved first, then, let them be ministering, being, unaccusable:
texts.1ti.3.11: Wives, in the same way,—dignified, not given to intrigue, sober, faithful in all things.
texts.1ti.3.12: Let, ministers, be husbands of, one wife, over children, presiding, well, and over their own houses;
texts.1ti.3.13: For, they who have ministered well, a good degree for themselves, are acquiring, and great freedom of speech in the faith that is in Christ Jesus.
texts.1ti.3.14: These things, unto thee, I am writing, hoping to come [unto thee] shortly,—
texts.1ti.3.15: But, if I should tarry, that thou mayest know—how it behoveth, in a house of God, to behave oneself,—the which, is an assembly of a Living God, a pillar and basement of the truth;—
texts.1ti.3.16: And, confessedly great, is the sacred secret of godliness,—Who was made manifest in flesh, was declared righteous in spirit, was made visible unto messengers, was proclaimed among nations, was believed on in the world, was taken up in glory.
texts.1ti.4.1: Howbeit, the Spirit, expressly saith—that, in later seasons, some will revolt from the faith, giving heed unto seducing spirits, and unto teachings of demons—
texts.1ti.4.2: in hypocrisy, speaking falsehood, [of demons] cauterised in their own conscience,—
texts.1ti.4.3: Forbidding to marry, [commanding] to abstain from foods which, God, created to be received with thanksgiving by them who believe and personally know the truth;
texts.1ti.4.4: Because, every creature of God, is good, and nothing to be cast away, if, with thanksgiving, it be received,—
texts.1ti.4.5: For it is hallowed by the word of God and intercession,
texts.1ti.4.6: These things, submitting to the brethren, thou shall be, a noble, minister of Christ Jesus, nourishing thyself with the words of the faith, and of the noble teaching which thou hast closely studied.
texts.1ti.4.7: But, from the profane and old-wives’ stories, excuse thyself, and be training thyself unto godliness;
texts.1ti.4.8: For, the bodily training, for little, is profitable, whereas, godliness, for all things is profitable,—having, promise, of life—the present and the coming.
texts.1ti.4.9: Faithful, the saying! and, of all acceptance, worthy;
texts.1ti.4.10: For, to this end, are we toiling and contending, because we have set our hope on a Living God, Who is Saviour of all men—specially, of such as believe.
texts.1ti.4.11: Be giving these things in charge, and be teaching:—
texts.1ti.4.12: Let, no one, despise, thy youth, but, an ensample, become thou of the faithful,—in discourse, in behaviour, in love, in faith, in chastity.
texts.1ti.4.13: While I am coming, be giving heed—to the reading, to the exhorting, to the teaching:
texts.1ti.4.14: Be not careless of the gift of favour, that is in thee, which was given thee through means of prophesying, along with a laying on of the hands of the eldership.
texts.1ti.4.15: These things, be thy care, in these things, be thou, that, thine advancement, may be, manifest, unto all:
texts.1ti.4.16: Be giving heed to thyself, and to thy teaching,—abide still in them; for, this doing, both, thyself, shalt thou save, and them that hearken to thee.
texts.1ti.5.1: An elderly man, do not thou reprimand, but beseech him, as [though he were thy] father,—younger men, as brothers,
texts.1ti.5.2: Elderly women, as mothers, younger women, as sisters, in all chastity.
texts.1ti.5.3: Widows, honour thou—who indeed are widows:—
texts.1ti.5.4: Howbeit, if, any widow, hath, children or grandchildren, let them be learning—first, unto their own house, to be shewing reverence, and, returns, to be making unto their progenitors; for, this, is acceptable before God;
texts.1ti.5.5: But, she who is indeed a widow, and is left alone, hath turned her hope towards God, and is giving attendance unto the supplications and the prayers, night and day,—
texts.1ti.5.6: Whereas, she that runneth riot, while living, is, dead:
texts.1ti.5.7: And, these things, be giving in charge, that, without reproach, they may be;
texts.1ti.5.8: If, however, anyone, for his own, and specially them of his household, taketh not forethought, his faith, hath he denied, and is worse, than one without faith!
texts.1ti.5.9: Let, a widow, be put on the list—having become, not less than sixty years old, one man’s, wife,
texts.1ti.5.10: In noble works, being well-attested;—if she hath nourished children, if she hath shewn hospitality, if, saints feet, she hath washed, if, them who were in tribulation, she hath succoured, if, in every good, work she hath followed on:
texts.1ti.5.11: But, younger widows, decline thou; for, as soon as they wax wanton against the Christ, to marry, are they determined,—
texts.1ti.5.12: Having, as sentence,—that, their first faith, they have set at nought;
texts.1ti.5.13: At the same time, to be idlers, are they learning, going about from house to house; and, not only idlers, but, gossips, also, and, busybodies,—saying the things they ought not,
texts.1ti.5.14: I am minded, therefore, that, the younger ones, marry, bear children, be mistress of the house,—giving, no single occasion, unto the opposer, as a cause, of reviling;
texts.1ti.5.15: For, already, some have turned aside after Satan:
texts.1ti.5.16: If any, believing woman, hath widows, let her be giving them succour, and not suffer the assembly to be burdened,—that, them who are indeed widows, it may itself succour.
texts.1ti.5.17: Let, the well presiding elders, of double honour, be accounted worthy, especially they who toil in discourse and teaching;
texts.1ti.5.18: For the scripture saith—A threshing ox, shalt thou not muzzle, and—Worthy, is the workman, of his hire.
texts.1ti.5.19: Against an elder, entertain not, an accusation, except at, [the mouth of] two, or three, witnesses;
texts.1ti.5.20: But, them who are sinning, before all, do thou reprove, that, the rest also, may have, fear:—
texts.1ti.5.21: I adjure thee, before God, and Christ Jesus, and the chosen messengers, that, these things, thou observe, apart from prejudgment, doing, nothing, by partiality.
texts.1ti.5.22: Hands, suddenly, upon no one, lay, neither have fellowship with sins of strangers: thyself, keep, chaste:—
texts.1ti.5.23: No longer, be a water-drinker, but, of a little wine, make use, because of thy stomach and thy, frequent, sicknesses.
texts.1ti.5.24: Some men’s sins, are, openly evident, leading on into judgment, with some, however, they even follow after;
texts.1ti.5.25: In the same way, the noble works also, are openly evident,—and, they that are otherwise, cannot be hid.
texts.1ti.6.1: Let, as many as are servants under a yoke, be counting, their own masters, worthy, of all honour, lest, the name of God and the teaching, be defamed.
texts.1ti.6.2: They, however, that have believing masters, let them not despise them, because they are, brethren but, the more, be doing them service, because, believing and beloved, are they who, from the good workmanship, receive advantage. These things, be teaching, and exhorting:—
texts.1ti.6.3: If anyone doth otherwise teach, and doth not adhere to healthful discourses—those of our Lord Jesus Christ, and to the teaching that is, according to godliness,
texts.1ti.6.4: He is beclouded, knowing, nothing, rightly, but is diseased about questionings, and word-battles—out of which spring envy, strife, defamations, wicked surmising,
texts.1ti.6.5: incessant quarrellings of men wholly corrupt in their mind and bereft of the truth,—supposing godliness to be, a means of gain!
texts.1ti.6.6: Now it is a great means of gain—godliness, with a sufficiency of one’s own;
texts.1ti.6.7: For, nothing, brought we into the world, neither, to take anything out, are we able;—
texts.1ti.6.8: And, having sustenance and covering, we shall be content;
texts.1ti.6.9: But, they who are determined to be rich, fall into temptation, and a snare, and many foolish and hurtful covetings, the which, sink men into ruin and destruction,—
texts.1ti.6.10: For, a root of all the vices, is the love of money, which, some, being eager for, have been seduced from the faith, and have pierced, themselves, about with many pangs.
texts.1ti.6.11: But, thou, O man of God! from these things, flee! and pursue righteousness, godliness, faith, love, endurance, meekness;
texts.1ti.6.12: Be contesting the noble contest of the faith,—lay hold of the age-abiding life—unto which thou wast called, and didst make the noble confession before many witnesses.
texts.1ti.6.13: I charge thee, before God, who engendereth life in all things, and Christ Jesus, who, before Pontius Pilate, witnessed the noble confession,
texts.1ti.6.14: That thou keep the commandment without spot, free from reproach, until the forthshining of our Lord Jesus Christ—
texts.1ti.6.15: Which, in its own fit times, the happy and only Potentate will shew—the King of them that reign, and Lord of them that wield lordship,
texts.1ti.6.16: Who alone hath immortality, dwelling in light unapproachable,—Whom no man hath seen—nor can see: unto whom, be honour and might age-abiding. Amen.
texts.1ti.6.17: Upon them who are rich in the present age, lay thou charge—not to be high-minded, nor to have set their hope on, riches’, uncertainty,—but on God, who offereth us all things richly for enjoying,
texts.1ti.6.18: To be doing good, to be rich in noble works, to be, generous in giving, ready for fellowship,—
texts.1ti.6.19: Treasuring up for themselves a good foundation for the future, that they may lay hold on the life [which is life] indeed.
texts.1ti.6.20: O Timothy! that which hath been entrusted, do thou guard, avoiding the profane pratings and oppositions of falsely named knowledge,—
texts.1ti.6.21: Which, some professing, concerning the faith, have missed the mark! Favour be with you.

texts.1ti.1.1: Pablo, apóstol de Jesucristo por mandato de Dios nuestro Salvador, y del Señor Jesucristo nuestra esperanza,
